doc.config_title: DC1-DC2 EVPN/VXLAN Multi-Site demo fabric (BGP only). Generated by fabric_design.
doc.classification: FICTIONAL DEMO DATA: not for any real network.
doc.summary:
Two independent Nexus EVPN/VXLAN fabrics, one per data center, joined by dedicated Multi-Site border gateways over a redundant routed DCI. Each site has 2 × Nexus 9500 spines (EVPN route servers), 4 × Nexus 9300 leafs in two vPC pairs and 2 × Nexus 93180YC-FX3 anycast BGWs, with a Palo Alto HA pair at the north-south edge.

BGP only: eBGP IPv4 underlay on the /31 links, MP-BGP L2VPN EVPN overlay (eBGP between loopbacks), eBGP to the firewalls, across the DCI and to AWS/Azure. BFD on every session.

  • Each site keeps all infrastructure inside its own /16 (10.110.0.0/16 for DC1, 10.120.0.0/16 for DC2), in the 10.x.240.0/21 block.
  • Only routed traffic crosses the DCI. Each site has its own L2VNIs; nothing is stretched by default.
  • AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute terminate on the BGWs in VRF TRUST at both sites.

current.intro: The demo assumes a typical starting point: a legacy core per site, routed to an HA firewall pair.
current.outro: VLAN N uses 10.110.N.0/24 at DC1 and 10.120.N.0/24 at DC2. The VNI numbering builds on it (§6).

doc.topology_caption: Per site: 2 spines (EVPN route servers), 4 leafs in two vPC pairs (LF-03/04 face the firewalls) and 2 Multi-Site BGWs. The DCI is a full mesh: carrier A (solid) joins the BGW-01s and the BGW-02s, carrier B (dashed) crosses over, so every BGW has one circuit on each carrier.
decisions: eBGP IPv4 unicast on /31 links, BFD, MTU 9216. Spines share one ASN per site; every leaf and BGW has its own
One protocol end to end; bestpath as-path multipath-relax for ECMP.
MP-BGP L2VPN EVPN, eBGP between loopbacks. Spines are route servers (retain RT all, next-hop unchanged)
With eBGP the spines can't be route reflectors.
Distributed anycast gateway, shared MAC 2020.0000.00aa, symmetric IRB
L2VNI = site base + VLAN: DC1 110000 + VLAN, DC2 120000 + VLAN
Site-local L2VNIs; reads as the site.
Auto RTs differ per leaf ASN.
Routed /29 transits to LF-03/LF-04, eBGP with BFD, ECMP on the firewall
Two carriers in a full mesh: every BGW has one circuit per carrier, to a different remote BGW; only BGW loopbacks in the DCI underlay
No single carrier, circuit or BGW failure isolates a BGW, and each site stays its own failure domain.
AWS DX and Azure ER on the BGWs in VRF TRUST, strict allowlists
Cloud prefixes cross the DCI as type-5 backup paths.
Dedicated anycast BGWs, two per site, on N9K-C93180YC-FX3: Eth1/49-50 to the spines, Eth1/51-52 DCI, Eth1/53-54 spare, AWS and Azure on their own SFP28 ports

Cisco's standard Multi-Site model: every BGW forwards, the site scales to more BGWs without redesign, and no vPC or endpoints sit on the BGWs. vPC BGW only fits when hosts must dual-home to the border; BGW-on-spine overloads the spines.
best_practice: Loopback0 for router-ID/peering, loopback1 for the VTEP, vPC anycast VTEP as secondary
BGP-only fabric: eBGP underlay, MP-BGP EVPN overlay between loopbacks
BFD on underlay, firewall, DCI and cloud sessions
Distributed anycast gateway, symmetric IRB, one L3VNI per VRF
vPC with advertise-pip and advertise virtual-rmac; backup underlay VLAN in system nve infra-vlans
Ingress replication. Multicast (PIM, anycast RP on the spines) is the NDFC default and scales better, but at 6 VTEPs per site IR is simpler and fully supported. Revisit beyond ~20 VTEPs or heavy BUM
Anycast BGW (not vPC BGW), fabric and DCI tracking, delay-restore
External connectivity per VRF with eBGP, no IGP redistribution
Default route only from the edge; never across the DCI
Manage with Nexus Dashboard Fabric Controller (NDFC)
Recommended for production: the BGP fabric and Multi-Site Domain templates generate equivalent configs and keep them in sync
doc.addressing_intro: Each site uses 10.x.240.0/21 for infrastructure. Both sites have the same layout, so swapping 110 for 120 maps DC1 to DC2.

tenants.dmz_intro: Only if the DMZ moves into the fabric: L2-only VNIs on LF-03/LF-04.
tenants.firewall_direct: Internet circuits and remote-access appliances stay on the firewalls.
tenants.vrf_note: VLANs 3900–3950 sit below the NX-OS reserved range (3968–4095).

doc.firewall: The firewalls connect to the border-service leafs with routed /29 links and eBGP (AS 65217 / 65227). They advertise only 0.0.0.0/0 and accept only the two site /16s, with ECMP across both leafs.

multisite.body:
Why block the default route: each firewall originates 0/0 into its own fabric only, so internet traffic never leaves through the other site's firewall.

AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute

  • BGW-01 carries DX connection 1 and the ER primary; BGW-02 carries DX connection 2 and the ER secondary.
  • Inbound: approved cloud CIDRs only. Outbound: own /16, plus the other site's /16 prepended as a backup.
multisite.allowlist_note: Example allowlists. Replace them with the VPC and VNet CIDRs that attach to your DX and ER gateways.

configs.intro: Complete configurations for all 16 switches, also written as files in configs/ next to this workbook.
configs.note: Demo only. Validate against your Nexus models and NX-OS release, and fill in every <placeholder>.

migration: Underlay, EVPN, NVE, L3VNI. Host SVIs created shut.
eBGP to the legacy core on VLAN 99 for the migration window.
Per VLAN: extend, move servers, then bring up the anycast SVI.
Apply the PAN-OS handoff file and re-cable to LF-03/LF-04.
Bring up the BGWs, DCI and cloud sessions.
tests: Traffic shifts to the other spine via ECMP
Every BGW keeps its carrier B circuit; all four BGWs stay in service at half the DCI capacity
show nve multisite dci-links, show bgp l2vpn evpn summary
Both BGW-01s stay in service on carrier B; their loopbacks reroute through the remote BGW-02 and fabric
The remote BGWs keep a circuit to BGW-02; DCI traffic moves to BGW-02 through the Multi-Site VIP
open_items: Spine and leaf models, port maps, NX-OS release. BGWs: N9K-C93180YC-FX3 (confirm optics for the DCI and the 10G cloud cross-connects).
DCI circuits (four for the full mesh, two per carrier), cloud circuits, VLAN IDs, MTU.
